claim: T-V10-52 (l.3094) cannot be built against V08's tier rule. Its fixture carries 'a plague condition withheld at public' and asserts 'the withheld plague absent at public from every read, request, reply, card and transcript'. Under V08 §3.16 (7) (e) (J-V8.128) and T-V8-59 (l.3226), 'a condition whose row gives a look is admitted at public and one whose row is none only at secret'; plague maps to quarantine (V11 §3.25.9), so a plague condition is public at every key. No mechanism in the set withholds a look-bearing condition, so the fixture asserts something the design forbids. V10 §3.23 row 34 ('a condition the key withholds') and V09's T-V9-85 clause ('under a player view a withheld condition is never drawn …', on a fixture of siege, refugees and plague) presuppose the same thing; they are vacuous rather than contradictory.
required_change: T-V10-52's knowledge clause reads: 'at public every look-bearing condition — the siege, the refugee wave and the plague — is listed with its name and weeks (V08 §3.16 (7) (e)); a none-row condition carried beside them (an infiltrated stressor) is named in no read, request, reply, card or transcript at public, and only at secret'. The fixture loses 'a plague condition withheld at public'. V10 §3.23 row 34's 'a condition the key withholds' reads 'a none-row condition, admitted only at secret'.

claim: The clerk's scratch commit resubmits filtered lists that §11.2 compares unfiltered. VAT-R1-03's fix makes V10 §3.5 step 3 (l.1450–1457) read the item from `preview(scratch, events, { filtered: true })`, then commit by `edit(scratch, events, { filtered: true })` 'with the preview's fates and renames filled, §11.2's resubmission form'. It adds: 'A commit that answers otherwise than its preview (a `conflict`, or a `confirm` whose fates differ) refuses the item with that answer and records the preview equality check's defect'. But the preview's lists are the filtered ones: §11.2 *`filtered`* renders fates and renames under the caller's key (a withheld place by address and kind, a concealed use and an unexcavated element absent). §11.2 *Confirming fates* commits a resubmission only 'when a fresh dry run computes the same fates and renames', and *Knowledge* states that a `confirm` result goes only to an editing role, unfiltered. So whenever the session's effective key withholds an entry of an item's fates or renames — under View as, or with a host-lowered editor key (V10 §2.3) — the engine answers `confirm`. The scratch cannot have moved between the two calls, so the difference is the filter's. Yet V10 refuses a lawful item and writes a `previewMismatch` defect. Round 1's text confirmed a scratch `confirm` at once, and V10 §4.2 (1) avoids the trap on the user's document by previewing unfiltered and comparing the filtered projection; step 3 no longer shares that rule.
required_change: V10 §3.5 step 3, after '§11.2's resubmission form, as V10 §4.2 (1) commits:', reads: 'a `confirm` answer — which a filtered resubmission receives wherever the session's key withholds an entry of the fates or renames (§11.2 *`filtered`*, *Confirming fates*) — is confirmed on the scratch at once, `confirm(scratch, token, fates, renames)` with that answer's own lists. A `confirm` result reaches an editing client unfiltered (§11.2 *Knowledge*), and the scratch is disposable. This holds whenever the filtered projection of the answer's lists at the session's effective key equals the preview's, compared as V10 §4.2 (1) compares (counts, fates by address, renames). Only a `conflict`, or a `confirm` whose projection differs, refuses the item with that answer and records the preview equality check's defect (V10 §2.8)'. T-V10-11's scratch clause adds a View as fixture whose declaration moves a concealed use and renames a withheld place: the item commits on the scratch and records no defect. J-V10.127 adds 'a filtered resubmission's `confirm` is confirmed with its own lists'.

claim: V10 §3.9a's damage part (l.1803–1808) restates the comparison as 'each plan element shown damaged once the building's decay level … reaches the element's one keyed threshold (§6.3's `plan.damage`, …), the one comparison every reader makes'. 'Reaches' without §6.3's 'above 0' reads as level ≥ t. With V11's lo = 0 that damages an element at level 0, which V10's own *Absent* bullet ('a building never decayed has none … `item123.damage`') and T-V10-53's no-op clause exclude. The text holds two readings of one rule, and it restates a rule whose home is §6.3.
required_change: V10 §3.9a: 'reaches the element's one keyed threshold (§6.3's `plan.damage`, within its element kind's range of V11's rows), the one comparison every reader makes' → 'is above 0 and at least the element's one keyed threshold — §6.3's comparison (`plan.damage`, within its element kind's range of V11's rows), the one every reader makes, so a level of 0 damages nothing'.
